google_reviews.text: We stayed there. We highly recommend it. The food is fantastic because it's all fresh daily. You absolutely have to eat there.

google_reviews.author: Gert-Jan Kiebert
google_reviews.text:
The setting of this agritourism is beautiful. The house and garden are full of character and create a lovely atmosphere for dinner.

Unfortunately, the hospitality and service did not meet our expectations. The entire service was handled by what appeared to be the owner’s 12-year-old son. We couldn’t tell whether he was helping voluntarily, but he didn’t seem to enjoy it and it made us feel a bit uncomfortable.

Another disappointment was that about half of the dishes on the menu were unavailable. We were only informed of this after some of our food had already been served, which made ordering and dining together difficult.

The location has a lot of potential, but with warmer hospitality, clearer communication, and better menu availability, the overall experience would be much better.

google_reviews.author: Jessica Römer
google_reviews.text: Hospitality is a top priority at this establishment. Even the twelve-year-old son—health and safety regulations in Albania are somewhat more lenient regarding child labor—knows how to make guests feel truly at ease. We ordered some traditional Albanian dishes and were taken on an interesting culinary journey, where garlic was not shied away from. But that was no problem, as we both ate it. Sitting in the garden is truly idyllic, just a little away from the hustle and bustle of the village center. Definitely worth a visit!

google_reviews.author: Berjan Geertjes
google_reviews.text: A super experience. Authentic Albanian, eco food from their own garden. What an experience, great atmosphere, really delicious dishes, a top-notch experience.

google_reviews.author: Emil Ryberg
google_reviews.text: Good traditional albanian, even if you eat vegetarian

reviews.author: Dagmar
reviews.text_en: More modest, but clean, nice accommodation. Very nice, friendly hosts, very accommodating. Excellent cuisine at a good price, breakfast, dinner. Nice location, starting point for most walking trips in the area . Close to shop, quiet in the evening. Would definitely recommend.

google_reviews.author: Adriana Ivankova
google_reviews.text: I need to report this guesthouse. We did the reservation 3 months in advance. On the day of the expected checkin, we did a 10hrs hike and after coming to Theth, the guesthouse owner told us that he has no reservation , even the house was full. This was very unpleasant situation. My friend broke a leg and in the evening coming for checkin the guy sent us away without place to stay. Please do not go there, if you dont want to have a destroyed vacay. Even the guy didnt speak English and didnt care much about the situation!

google_reviews.author: Kamil Dzurovčin
google_reviews.text: We had a reservation, after 8 hours of hiking after arriving at the hostel they told us that the hostel was full, be very careful with this accommodation, we regret that we did not read the reviews on Google sooner!!!

google_reviews.author: Lisa Felice
google_reviews.text:
Man oh man we were so disappointed after finishing a 16km hike from Valbona to Theth. I blame it on a last minute booking, making it the only affordable place. But when entering the room, the smell was hard to ignore and a lot of things were broken or need replacement (toilet seat, lights). The beds were also the worst we encountered on our 2.5week trip through Albania. Old, saggy and with an unhygienic undertone. When showering, the entire bathroom gets wet - though a lot of accommodations in Albania seem to have this :’).
The breakfast and outside seating were the two better aspects of this stay.
We also noticed mold in the bathroom the next morning.
In short: would not recommend

google_reviews.author: Meike Bakker
google_reviews.text: We booked the deluxe room with balcony, but upon arrival the guy didn’t even seem to know we were coming. He didn’t ask for our reservation or name, just asked how many nights we were staying and assigned us a room. The room had no balcony and not all of the listed amenities. There was also nothing deluxe about the room, the power was not working all the time (the lights were flickering or randomly went out, the sockets did not work all the time, fridge was not working) and the aircon had no remote and started beeping randomly. Eventually the power was working, but the fridge only started working 1,5 days later. When we addressed the issues to the owner, he said this was the right room and we were dismissed. The beds were also horrible, we were literally lying on the strings of the bed, really hard and uncomfortable. It also was creaking really badly. We both woke up with a sore back. The dogs also bark all night and the curtains do not fully close, and the front door has no curtains, so you have to cover your eyes if you don’t want to wake up at the break of dawn. The only thing we appreciated was the breakfast and the location, they made us a little breakfast package our first day because we were leaving early, which we really appreciated, and the breakfast on the second day was also really nice. Still nice people but not a good experience for us overall.

google_reviews.author: Kay
google_reviews.text:
We had a really nice time in Theth, but the accommodation had a few flaws.

The location of the accommodation is great. The accommodation we booked was the villa/lodge. The toilet seat was loose and the water didn't drain properly, causing the bathroom to be constantly flooded. As a result, you couldn't go to the toilet or freshen up at the sink without getting wet feet. The power went out on one of the two nights (so did the air conditioning, which was connected to two large batteries), and the front door jams against the floor, making a shrill, high-pitched sound when opening and closing the door. Power outages are a known problem throughout Theth, and they tried to repair the front door but to no avail.

Finally, the cottage is situated under a tree from which "acorns" fall onto the corrugated iron roof all the time. You hear this several times during the day and multiple times at night while sleeping, which can disturb your night's rest. Additionally, there is no mini-fridge, coffee maker, etc.

The accommodation doesn't have to be special, as you will be spending a lot of time outdoors in Theth, but it really could be better.

google_reviews.author: Johanna Redwood
google_reviews.text:
Great customer service from the time we arrived. The receptionist was friendly, welcoming and very good at answering to all our needs. The cleaning staff from the Phillipines were so friendly, always laughing and cheerful making it a great atmosphere. The room we were in was lovely. Very comfortable bed and pillows. Great size, excellent shower (though my husband had a cold shower the second night- I think the whole town has a problem with electricity) a shower separate to the toilet which is lacking in Albania!
Only downside was there was no air con or no fan. It was hot. We left the windows open but due to other guests screaming and talking very loudly and also guests smoking outside our room (another common occurrence and complaint we have) we had to close them.
Definitely would stay there again. Beautiful views.
We ate at the restaurant- the review will be under Hotel Alpeth.

google_reviews.text: Beware! Dozens of bed bugs were crawling around (see video). I awoke at night from all the itching. When I went to ask some of the staff at the restaurant at night, they just laughed, and found it incredibly funny. They were clearly intoxicated and very rude. Next morning I mentioned the bed bug problem to the receptionist, and he just shrugged it off as if its normal. No refund or apology, nothing. Awful experience...

google_reviews.text:
A nice but not very functional hotel for us. We had a room with 5 boys (with the possibility for 6). The beds were good, and besides a shower and toilet, that was the only thing present in the room.

There was no signal in the apartment, although this was not bothersome.

google_reviews.author: Evie Porter
google_reviews.text: Had an absolutely delicious dinner here. Everything in the set menu tasted delicious and fresh, with an option for the three vegetarians in our party which didn't feel lacking at all. The quality of the fish was also fantastic, but most importantly the service was fantastic! The staff were enthusiastic and kind, giving tips for the rest of our trip, with special thanks to our waiter Erikson, who lent his coat to a member of our party who was cold! Truly above and beyond :)

google_reviews.author: Marie-Soleil Cordeau
google_reviews.text:
I absolutely loved my stay. It felt very authentic and gave me a wonderful taste of Albanian hospitality. The atmosphere was warm and welcoming, and I immediately felt comfortable there.

The house was very clean, including the two shared bathrooms, which were surprisingly spotless despite being shared by several guests. The beds were comfortable, and the communal dining tables made it easy to meet other travelers and share stories.

There was plenty of delicious food, and the breakfast was excellent.

There was a small issue in our dorm, as water from the bathroom above was dripping onto one of the beds. It wasn’t an issue for me personally, but it was unfortunate for the person sleeping there.

Overall, I absolutely loved my night at Rupa Guest House. It was one of those places where I simply felt good being there. I would happily stay again!

google_reviews.author: Clemens N
google_reviews.text: Good food, nice people.

google_reviews.author: Liv Coates
google_reviews.text:
Upon arrival the host wasn’t the friendliest. She had us wait for an hour with no information given as to what was happening and made us feel like we’d booked the wrong room. We had booked a double room but she seemed surprised that we wanted to be together.

We were put in a very small attic room where you can only stand up in the centre which was a struggle for my partner and would be for anyone taller than 5”10. We also felt very claustrophobic as we couldn’t put our stuff anywhere neatly.

The shared bathroom was mouldy and smelt of sewage. I felt dirtier coming out of the bathroom than I did before showering. There is often no toilet roll. As a woman, the small curtain used to provide privacy was very uncomfortable as anyone tall can see straight into the bathroom and it could easily be moved aside as it was on the outside. Having a shower also caused everything in there to be soaked.

Considering dinner and breakfast are paid for separately, it is not worth eating here as you don’t get your own portion and she gave some guests more food if she appeared to speak with them more.

We have stayed in many places on our 2 month backpacking trip but the standards of cleanliness and the overall hostility made us not want to stay again.

google_reviews.author: Rumi
google_reviews.text:
Overall, it's a very comfortable and relaxing mountain cabin.

The only drawback is that the bathroom facilities are a bit insufficient (two rooms).

Because there are also campers, there are sometimes wait times, and sometimes there's no hot water.

If you order breakfast or dinner, you'll share it with other guests.

The internet signal and electricity sometimes drop, but overall it's very good – just consider it a power outage in the mountains 🤣

google_reviews.text: We ordered a risotto and tagliatelle. The food was actually really good, unlike other restaurants in Theth that are supposedly “the best”. Moreover, it was really cheap: less than €10 pp for dinner+drinks. Because of the surrounding camping area (no buildings), the view is stunning all around. And of course, the waiter and other staff (the family) are really friendly to customers and clearly enjoy working together.

google_reviews.text:
Kompleksi Zorgji in Theth is a wonderful place to stay if you want to experience the beauty and hospitality of the Albanian Alps. The location is breathtaking, surrounded by mountains and nature, and the atmosphere is peaceful and authentic. The rooms are comfortable and clean, and the staff are incredibly friendly and welcoming. Everything felt warm, genuine, and well taken care of.

A perfect place to relax, enjoy the stunning scenery, and experience Theth at its best. Highly recommended! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Ps. To be mentioned,  Daniela is the best from all the people working in there.

reviews.author: Ema Bulirova
reviews.text_en: The campsite has many flat spots for pitching a tent. It is simply equipped: a sink for washing dishes, a few tables, three showers with toilets. They are clean, but without toilet paper. Hot water flows for 2 hours in the morning and 3 in the evening. It is possible to use the toilet in the restaurant, which belongs to the campsite. They are more equipped.

reviews.author: Jakub Štěrba
reviews.text_en: Spacious campsite. The toilets are simple, but you can go right next door to the restaurant belonging to the campsite, where they are new and luxurious. Friendly service.

reviews.text_en: Nice place, clean campsite but the services - the toilets aren't great cleanliness, shower only cold water, barking and movement of foreign dogs at night and WiFi very slow.

reviews.author: Stany M
reviews.text_en: Hot water only from 5 PM to 8 PM, electricity for charging is not working in some places, the wifi dropped out on us, fortunately on the last day, beautiful surroundings, level area for tents, volleyball court with gravel, toilets only 2 cabins with shower without toilet paper. Basic things are here, but it is nothing special.

reviews.text_en: Great campsite, facilities, location, plenty of space, WiFi, a restaurant is part of the campsite.

reviews.author: Jan Jiránek
reviews.text_en: Accommodation in a tent on a meadow behind the restaurant. 10 Euros per night for two people. An additional 5 Euros per night if you have a car. The bathrooms are nice with hot showers.

reviews.text_en:
Bitten by dog & gear damaged!

The campsite has a dog that bite me and damaged my brand new ultralight tent. Owners didn’t seem to care at all even after I was screaming for help. I honestly never write bad reviews because I feel bad for small business owners. But this is a matter of safety. They offered to shoot the dog in a mocking tone as a solution. Camp somewhere else, there are lots of better options.

google_reviews.text:
One of the worst shopping experiences I have had. This market seems to find every possible way to make customers pay more than they should. I was extremely disappointed to find out that they charge an additional 200 lek just for paying by card. This is completely unacceptable and feels like an unnecessary extra charge imposed on customers.

What makes it even worse is the exchange rate they use for euros. They take euros at a rate that is significantly lower than the actual market/exchange rate, so customers lose money simply because they choose to pay in euros. When you combine the unfair exchange rate with the additional card fee, the whole experience feels incredibly dishonest and unfair.

The staff should clearly inform customers about these additional charges and the exchange rate before taking payment. Customers should not have to discover these costs at the checkout. A business should be transparent about its prices and payment conditions instead of taking advantage of customers who may not notice the difference.

Honestly, I left feeling completely ripped off. There are plenty of other places where you can shop without being charged unnecessary fees and given such an unfavorable exchange rate. I would strongly recommend avoiding this market and choosing another place instead. Definitely not coming back.

We had a really lovely stay at Guesthouse Bec Villi in Theth. The guesthouse is in a peaceful spot surrounded by mountains, and the views are honestly spectacular, especially from the outdoor terrace. After a long day of hiking, it was exactly what we needed, a quiet, comfortable, and welcoming. The bed was surprisingly comfortable and made it very easy to get a good night’s sleep. Everything was clean and well looked after, and the family running the guesthouse were genuinely friendly and helpful without being overbearing.

What really made the stay special was the atmosphere. It feels like a proper family-run guesthouse rather than a standard hotel, which gives it a lot of charm. Sitting outside in the evening with the mountains all around was definitely one of the highlights of our time in Theth. The location is a little away from the centre, but that also means it’s peaceful and the views are much better. I would happily stay here again and would definitely recommend it to anyone visiting Theth, especially if you want beautiful scenery, comfortable beds, and a warm, authentic Albanian welcome. 🤗

One small suggestion: it would be great to have some healthier breakfast options, as quite a lot of it was deep-fried. The cash-only policy is a bit of a downside, but the hosts were incredibly helpful about it – they even walked us to a friend’s place nearby that had a card terminal so we could get cash.

Overall, a wonderful stay full of charm, and we’d happily recommend it.

Even though the staff was friendly, we feel a bit tricked. See details below.

UPDATE after the owner's response:

Unfortunately, several statements in the owner's response are factually incorrect, so I would like to clarify them.

First, the €70 price did not include dinner. We had already eaten dinner down in Theth before the owners picked us up around midnight. We did not receive any dinner at the guesthouse, and the owners know this. Therefore, the statement that the €70 consisted of €50 for the room plus €20 for dinner is simply false.

Secondly, the room door could not be locked from the inside. We tried. I specifically examined both the lock and the key, and the shape of the key does not allow it to be inserted and used from the inside. This was not a misunderstanding of how the lock worked.

Everything else described in my original review is also an accurate account of our stay: there was no electricity from the power outlets in our room, we only had cold water for showering in the evening, two of the three beds showed clear signs of woodworm activity, and there was a leaking bag of sawdust stored in the wardrobe.

I stand by my original review and all factual statements made in it. I am adding this update because the owner's response gives future guests an inaccurate impression of what actually happened during our stay.

I arrived at Lindi’s place at 8pm on the last day of a 7-day hike, completely out of cash thanks to some poor planning on my part. Rather than turn me away, my hostess Drita called her son in the UK to translate. In the middle of the Albanian Alps, on patchy internet, I somehow managed to transfer money to him, a lifesaver, since nowhere up in the mountains takes card.

What followed was a feast - Coca-Cola, fresh bread, homemade cheese, eggs from their own chickens, fries from their potato patch, salad from the garden, sausages, and more. The whole family were warm and endlessly accommodating. When I mentioned I’d be leaving at 5am, they packed me a picnic breakfast and by then it was pushing 10pm.

Drita’s husband walked me up to the guesthouse at the top of the hill, a simple room with three comfortable beds, a proper separate shower and toilet downstairs, and a balcony perfect for a post-hike drink and smoke under an unpolluted mountain sky. There was a bar underneath too, well-stocked and clearly lively in the evenings, though I was up and out too early to see it in full swing.

Huge thanks to Drita, her husband, and Adrien their son for feeding and housing one slightly underprepared British hiker. Your kindness and home-cooked food were exactly what I needed after a week of solo hiking. It goes without saying that if you’re looking at guesthouses around here, you know the scenery is otherworldly. From the guesthouses on top of the hill you can see a 360 degrees of beautiful mountains and also you get 4g, so a nice opportunity to call home. Can’t recommend enough. I sadly didn’t take any photos.

A wonderful mountain stay with a genuinely caring host

We had a very enjoyable stay at Bujtina Malaj and would definitely recommend it to anyone visiting the Valbonë Valley.
The host was exceptionally welcoming and attentive. He regularly checked if everything was alright and made sure we were comfortable throughout our stay. His local recommendations were incredibly valuable. After noticing that we had a 4x4 vehicle, he even marked a parking spot on a map that allowed us to start the Valbonë–Theth hike much closer to the trailhead with our children. That advice made a real difference for us.
The location is outstanding. The guesthouse is surrounded by forest with spectacular mountain views, making it a beautiful place to relax, especially during breakfast.
Breakfast was excellent, with freshly prepared omelettes, delicious homemade wild strawberry jam, great coffee, and tea for the children. It was a perfect start to each day.
The room had a very pleasant indoor climate. As the entire house is built from wood, it stayed naturally cool and was easy to ventilate, even during warmer days. The beds were comfortable, and the bunk bed included a safety rail, making it a great choice for families with children. Parking was easy and available directly in front of the property. The final stretch of road is unpaved, but compared to many other gravel roads we experienced in Albania, it was in very good condition.

Room for improvement:
The cleanliness of the room could have been a little better. Nothing was seriously wrong, and everything worked as expected, but this is one area where the accommodation could still improve.

Overall, this is a lovely place to stay with an outstanding host, a fantastic location, and a warm, authentic atmosphere. We would happily stay here again and highly recommend it to anyone visiting the Valbonë Valley.

The hotel is located at the end of the road, which makes it a peaceful place to stay. You can also enjoy a beautiful walk along the road, surrounded by stunning mountain scenery.

One small detail that could be improved is the lack of face towels in the room.

Unfortunately, however, our experience at the restaurant was quite disappointing. We asked the waiter whether the lamb or the goat meat was better, and based on his recommendation, we chose the lamb. Sadly, the meat arrived pre-prepared and not warm at all. The portion of flija we ordered was also disappointing—it was not really a proper serving, but seemed to consist mainly of the edges of the tray left over from its preparation.

It is a real shame because the location is fantastic, the nature is absolutely beautiful, and the hotel itself is very well designed and maintained. However, the restaurant unfortunately takes away from the overall experience due to the quality and presentation of the food.

A beautiful place with incredible nature and a lovely hotel, but the restaurant definitely needs improvement.

Truly the most wonderful place I have ever stayed in. Mark and his family are incredibly hospitable. The food is AMAZING and they are extremely generous with the portions. Since Mark and his daughter’s English was a bit rusty, communication was very short. Through a mix of Italian, Spanish, and English we discovered that Mark and his family had come back to the guesthouse earlier than usual to accommodate my brother and, which surprised us and warmed our hearts. Yes you can stay in a larger more modern hotel with heating and other amenities, but this small, cozy, family-run home stay will always rank better in my opinion. To book our stay we texted Mark through WhatsApp.

Also side note on directions:
Google Maps will lead you into some people’s backyards to get to the guest house. It tells you to take ‘Ruga Quki i Dunishes’ the whole way. The people living along the road were kind and pointed us in the right direction. However, instead of walking through their property you can go left at the dried river bed and find the wooden gate marked with the x in the picture below. Go through the gate and follow the dirt driveway to the house.

google_reviews.text: In a stunning location midway down into Valbonë from the end of the Theth-Valbonë trail, overlooking the (currently dry) river bed. Hospitality is warm and generous, food is excellent drawing on their farm produce - especially sheep’s cheese made from the sheep we saw being herded past the dining room on our first night! Petulla at breakfast and byrek at dinner were the best we had in Albania so far. The perfect peaceful place for R&R before and after hiking. Comfortable rooms, good showers and quick wi-fi. NB: cash only!

google_reviews.author: Napo
google_reviews.text:
We had a wonderful stay at Guesthouse Lazër Çardaku during our Peaks of the Balkans hike. From the moment we arrived, the family made us feel genuinely welcome. The guesthouse is surrounded by incredible mountain scenery and has such a peaceful atmosphere — exactly what you hope to find after spending a full day on the trail.

Our room was very clean, spacious, and comfortable, and we appreciated being able to properly rest and recharge. The homemade food was another highlight. Dinner and breakfast were fresh, plentiful, and delicious, and exactly the kind of meal you want before or after a long day of hiking.

What really stood out was the hospitality. The family was kind, attentive, and very helpful with everything we needed as hikers. Having people who understand the trail and the needs of hikers makes a tremendous difference on a trip like this.

The location is also excellent for exploring Valbonë and continuing along the Peaks of the Balkans. We loved being able to enjoy the mountain views and peaceful surroundings while still having everything we needed for the next day's hike.

A beautiful family-run guesthouse with wonderful people, excellent homemade food, comfortable rooms, and spectacular surroundings. We would happily stay here again and wholeheartedly recommend it to anyone hiking through Valbonë.

google_reviews.text:
If you are staying in Valbona, especially if you are doing the Valbona → Theth hike, please stay here. I genuinely cannot recommend Guesthouse Dardani enough.

From the moment we arrived, the host and her family welcomed us so openly and warmly into their home. They were some of the most genuinely kind, generous and accommodating people we have met on our entire trip. What could have simply been a place to sleep became one of the most special parts of our time in Albania.

The food, Breakfast, lunch and dinner were all absolutely incredible. Traditional and clearly made with so much love. Our entire group agreed that the hospitality and food alone made this place unforgettable.

The location is also perfect if you’re doing the Valbona–Theth hike. The trailhead is not far away, and you can pay a little extra for transport to the start if you don’t want to walk there. They can also prepare a packed lunch for the hike for around €6, which was so convenient. Otherwise, everything we needed was included.

There is also a beautiful river a short walk in the opposite direction where you can go for a swim, and the surrounding mountains and scenery are absolutely incredible. The guesthouse itself is surrounded by gardens and flowers, and when we visited there were the cutest puppies. There happened to be a meteor shower while we were staying, and the family let us take chairs and blankets outside so our whole group could sit together and watch the stars throughout the night.

The rooms are comfortable, each has its own ensuite, and there is Wi-Fi.

We left feeling incredibly grateful for the kindness and hospitality we were shown, and I genuinely wish we could have stayed longer.

10/10. One of the most memorable stays of my entire trip. 🇦🇱❤️

I loved staying here, would definitely go back, and 100% recommend it to anyone looking for a special getaway.

google_reviews.author: Massimo Deligios
google_reviews.text: The Bujtina is small but comfortable, with a dining room with a view. The wifi works well, and the room was very spacious. Dinner was a set menu and included chicken, burek, and salad for 11 euros. Breakfast was included and was plentiful, with bread, jam, and an omelet and sausage. There's also the option of a packed lunch, which I probably would have avoided because it included some vegetables, slices of bread, and a raw sausage for 5 euros. It's a bit far from the start of the trek, but it's easily manageable.

google_reviews.author: Rental Cars (Rental Cars Tirana)
google_reviews.text:
We had an absolute dream of a weekend staying at Bujtina Arturi in Valbona!
​The location is stunning, surrounded by vibrant greenery, majestic old pine trees, and lush green grass everywhere you look. Plum trees and wild berries line the area, and the mountain air was so fresh and clean that I honestly feel 10 years younger!
​The hosts were wonderful and so welcoming. They even have vans to organize guided trips to nearby canyons and waterfalls, making exploring the area super easy. On top of that, the breakfast was delicious and amazing each morning.
​To top it all off, the price was significantly more affordable compared to other accommodations in the region—incredible value for such a peaceful, beautiful experience.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ An excellent stop after the Theth-Valbona trek!

We stayed at Centerpark Valbona as part of our tour of the Albanian Alps with Miki Tours / Shala River Trip.

After about 16 km of hiking from Theth, including crossing the mountain pass and nearly 1,200 m of elevation gain, we were very happy to arrive at Centerpark Valbona! 😊
The resort is very pleasant, the rooms are comfortable, and the surroundings are simply magnificent, nestled in the Valbona mountains. After a long day of hiking, it's truly wonderful to be able to relax in a peaceful place and enjoy this stunning setting.

The location is also very convenient for continuing the trek, as the bus picks us up directly the next day to continue to Shala River.

A great stop for hikers crossing from Theth to Valbona, but also for anyone who simply wants to enjoy the beautiful Valbona Valley.

Highly recommended! 🇦🇱⛰️🥾

Breezy Hotel in Valbona is one of those places that is difficult to describe with words. 🏔️❤️ From the very first moment, you feel a special atmosphere where the beauty of nature, peace, elegance, and genuine hospitality come together perfectly.

The surroundings are stunning, the food is fantastic, and the service is truly exceptional. But what impressed us the most was the warmth and attention of the staff — they make you feel genuinely welcomed and valued throughout your stay.

Breezy is not simply a hotel where you stay… it is a place where you create memories you will want to experience all over again.

We stayed on the upper floor of the annex to the owner's house in a large room with sloping walls. There is a large bed consisting of two wide single beds pushed together, which is incredibly comfortable to sleep in.

Downstairs is a clean bathroom with a toilet and a bidet. The whole setup includes very reliable Wi-Fi.

You can park your car across the grass close to the hostess's house, and the gate is hermetically sealed all day long.

You can have dinner with the owner in the evening. You get a very generous portion, and all the Albanian food she prepares tastes exquisite.

The breakfast she offers in the morning is also fantastic. For example, there are delicious homemade treats and super tasty homemade jam.

The owner is a fantastic woman who goes to great lengths to make your stay enjoyable. Even though we were here for just one night, I would recommend it to everyone.

The view is also incredible! Extremely comfortable bed and it was nice being a little bit outside of Valbone.
If you want a local experience with a warm host- stay here! If you’re vegan or have dietary restrictions she does her best to accommodate all of them but also remember you’re in rural Albania and as a visitor you should respect their way of life. Don’t be a turist budalla! Much love, Drita! See you next time. Chris from Canada

google_reviews.author: Stephany gonzalez reyes
google_reviews.text: We stayed with Drita! And the spot was outstanding, clean, authentic, and with everything we needed! I would stay here and you should stay here if you can and you love nature! Also, this is a cultural exchange so be open to learn about Albanian culture, agriculture,  and food! Be open to exploring what Albanian cuisine is! This bed and breakfast offered a breakfast, which is a cultural immersion ( please appreciate it). This was my favourite location during my whole time in Albania. Thank you Drita! Stephany from Colombia will come back.

google_reviews.author: Daniel Honig
google_reviews.text: Lovely guesthouse! The rooms are beautiful, the views are out of this world, and the host is friendly and an amazing cook. She catered to our vegan needs, and cooked everything from her own garden. Highly recommend this guesthouse in Valbona

google_reviews.author: Liam Sid

A big tip on getting there - follow the signs to Bujtina Sherifaj. It is bang next door .

google_reviews.text:
One of the most beautiful and memorable places I’ve stayed in. The family is incredibly kind, welcoming, and helpful — they genuinely make you feel at home.

The rooms are beautiful, traditional, and incredibly cozy, but the garden is what completely stole my heart. 🌿 It’s absolutely gorgeous, surrounded by greenery and mountains, with vegetables, fruits, and so much life growing everywhere. It feels like a little piece of paradise.

And the food was absolutely incredible. Everything was so fresh and full of flavour, with vegetables picked straight from their own garden. You can genuinely taste the freshness and care that goes into the food. The meals felt homemade in the best possible way — rich, authentic, generous, and incredibly satisfying.

I honestly didn’t want to leave — I could live in this garden forever! 😄

If you’re looking for somewhere peaceful, authentic, cozy, surrounded by nature, and with genuinely wonderful hospitality and food, I couldn’t recommend this place enough. This is the kind of place you leave already thinking about when you can come back. ❤️

Definitely one of those places you leave already wanting to come back. ❤️

Since the property operates under two names, Guesthouse Relax and Guesthouse Niko, and the payment arrangements seem to vary depending on the booking, the pricing felt quite inconsistent.

For what you get, I personally felt it was overpriced. I would choose a different place if I were to return to the area.

google_reviews.author: Napo
google_reviews.text:
We had a fantastic stay at Guesthouse Kujtim Gocaj while hiking the Peaks of the Balkans. The location is absolutely perfect for hikers, surrounded by mountains and positioned conveniently along the route, which makes arriving after a demanding day feel especially rewarding.

The guesthouse has a relaxed, welcoming family atmosphere. Our accommodation was comfortable, and having a good shower and somewhere peaceful to rest after many hours on the trail made a huge difference. We also loved the outdoor areas, where you can sit, relax, and simply enjoy being surrounded by the Albanian Alps.

The traditional food was another highlight. After hiking all day, nothing beats sitting down to a generous home-cooked meal. Breakfast before starting the next stage and having food available for the trail were also extremely helpful. The guesthouse offers traditional meals and caters particularly well to people walking this route.

Most importantly, we appreciated the warmth and hospitality of the family. Staying in family-run guesthouses like this became one of our favorite parts of the Peaks of the Balkans experience.

A peaceful, comfortable, and authentic mountain stay in a fantastic location. We would happily recommend Guesthouse Kujtim Gocaj to anyone hiking through Çerem.

Rooms: Comfortable and peaceful, with everything we needed to recover after hiking. Having a good shower after a long trail day was especially appreciated.

Nearby activities: Fantastic location for hiking and enjoying the Albanian Alps. It is particularly convenient for people walking the Peaks of the Balkans.

Safety: Quiet, peaceful, and welcoming. We felt very comfortable staying here.

Walkability: One of its biggest advantages. The guesthouse is directly along the hiking route above Çerem, making it extremely convenient for arriving and departing on foot.

Food & drinks: Traditional, generous food that was perfect after hiking. Breakfast and having food available for the following day's trail made the stay especially convenient.

Noteworthy details: The combination of location, family hospitality, mountain views, outdoor seating, and traditional food makes this a great hikers' guesthouse. It feels like a genuine part of the Peaks of the Balkans experience rather than simply overnight accommodation.

google_reviews.author: Luuk Peters
google_reviews.text: A beautiful guesthouse with a view of the valley. The owners are a family with three generations handling the maintenance and preparing the meals. What I love about it is the combination of great facilities and a traditional, authentic Albanian experience, including Albanian food. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Sofie Glacová
reviews.text_en: Excellent accommodation. You can eat outside or inside, plus pay for a package: dinner, breakfast, lunch to go (with accommodation around 30€ per person). Dinner is hearty, breakfast as well, and the lunch package is enough for the whole day. We didn't drink the water here due to a previous epidemic of some illness, but bottled water can be bought here. They have new sanitary facilities. It has grown a lot here in recent years.

reviews.author: Roie
reviews.text_en:
Leonard's Guesthouse is a wonderful spot that provides everything a mountain lover needs when trekking the Balkans. It features clean and comfortable rooms, with electricity available until 11 PM. The toilets and showers have hot water, plenty of toilet paper, soap, and shampoo. They serve an excellent dinner with second helpings, and a good breakfast (a bit more variety would be a nice touch). There are water taps available, and you can buy bottled mineral water for €2. There is also a great area for tents. Truly everything a hiker could ask for.
Without a doubt, this place deserves a high rating, and I hope they keep it up!

This is a charming and very rustic place in a beautiful setting, right near a waterfall and a great spot for swimming. The whole valley is absolutely beautiful.

I was lucky enough to have one of the rooms with a proper bed, and it was very comfortable. The room was clean, and the showers were really good. Some of the other accommodations are much more basic, with mattresses on the floor under a sloped roof, so keep that in mind when booking.

The man who runs the place is incredibly kind and welcoming, which made my stay even more enjoyable.

The portions at dinner are generous, but the food could definitely be improved. Dinner is vegetarian, and I didn’t find the meals particularly tasty. The hard-boiled egg in the packed lunch was also consistently overcooked. On the other hand, the bread in the packed lunch was always fresh, which I really appreciated.

There is very little shade around the property, with not many places to sit and escape the sun.

Overall, I enjoyed my stay. Beautiful, rustic, clean and welcoming.

We ended up here by pure chance : the place a little further we were supposed to stay had overbooked us. I remembered, when walking by, the kid was asking if we needed a room. So I went back and luckily they still had the room. It was a small building next to the main building, in fact the lady told us we were the first to stay there and yep, it smelled brand new.
Room was very small, basically just the 2 beds but it was comfy, the shower was grand, there was a cosy living room and it had a lovely terrace, all to be shared with the people staying in a 2nd room.
But the dinner... waw, that was something else : there was an oven and a stove on the terrace where we sat so we saw the yummy homemade dinner being prepared right next to us. It didn't just look good, it tasted even better. What a treat !
On top : the trail to Plav starts just in front.
So we ended up here by chance but things always happen for a reason : what a discovery Mirsad's was !

google_reviews.text: Triangle Woodhouse is an excellent place to stay along the Peaks of the Balkans trail. The food is delicious and plentiful, the atmosphere is very cozy, and there are hot showers. Agron and his volunteers are generally very dedicated to making your stay as pleasant as possible and help wherever they can – whether it's with taxi services, border permits, or anything else. google_reviews.author: Wim Vansteelant
google_reviews.text:
Unfortunately our experience wasn't so good :-(
Hiking the PoB (Peaks of the Balkan) mid June, I had booked end of 2025 via Whatsapp. I confirmed again a week or 2 before we would be there. All good.
The day of the booking, after a hard day of hiking, we arrive... to be told there's no room for us. I could see my name and reservation in the book but seems they still overbooked.
Then we had to wait for the owner (Agron) to come over, he looked for another place almost next door but we found it to be so-so.
Luckily we had passed a cool place earlier (Mirsad's) so while waiting I had already popped over there and checked availability so we moved there.
To be fair, Agron did drive us there (ok, it was not far at all) and he had arranged our border permits but I hope he will tackle this internally. Still, everything happens for a reason : Mirsad's was bliss so we were happy chappies in the end.

google_reviews.text:
We visited this restaurant with our group of six and had an amazing experience. From the moment we walked in, the calm and relaxing atmosphere immediately helped us unwind after a long day of hiking.

As soon as we sat down, a member of staff welcomed us with the menus and asked if we would like something to drink. Throughout the entire meal, the staff were incredibly friendly, attentive, and accommodating, which made the experience even more enjoyable.

All six of us ordered different dishes, and every single one was excellent. Not only were the portions extraordinarily generous, but the food was also absolutely delicious. We were all very satisfied with our meals.

Overall, I would highly recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting Plav. It is the perfect place to enjoy a delicious and filling meal after a long day of hiking, but it is just as worth visiting if you are simply exploring the town!

Escape to the mountains in mid-August.
Overjoyed, my husband and I, guided by the reviews and pictures on Booking, find the number and call.

The first impression is mediocre.
The guy in the middle of Montenegro refuses to talk (he doesn't know his native language) we speak in English.
Thinking that we will be accommodated in the room we saw on Booking, we didn't even think that there was anything else.
However, there is.
So ask them to send you photos before booking.
Room 2 is falling apart.
Old beds, 2 separate and two on the floor, that wasn't such a big problem, they were comfortable and the bathroom was clean but falling apart.
The tiles around the sink are loose and filled with foam, the ceiling is falling apart from moisture, they haven't even painted it and you can see the patches and holes.
Broken tap and shower that sprays everywhere and the water heater is leaking water in the bathroom.
The carpet smells nice of moisture but the peak was in the evening. You travel half a day, half a day in the mountains, you come to sleep, you expect peace and the owner with his company and staff right under the window made a gathering of laughter, shouting, shouting....
I will praise the father, a hardworking man, he makes fresh pancakes at dawn, the breakfast is satisfying.
I took pictures of everything I wrote because I was very angry.... I cooled down and I don't want more of this.
But so that someone doesn't go through the same thing, ask everything in advance.

google_reviews.author: MISHA YASNO
google_reviews.text:
It was practically a scene from "Brigada": an Escalade, a Jeep, and a Hummer roll onto the grounds of Guest House Ropojan, and we roll out—the baker's dozen in "Prokletije."

It's a nearly 30-minute drive off-road, and at first it's unclear why the guesthouse is there, but then it dawns on you: this is a "hop-off airfield"—a transit stop where travelers can use a clean toilet, take a hot shower, and enjoy a warm stew lovingly prepared by the hosts on a modern wood-burning stove.

Everything is still brand new, uninhabited: in some places the lights don't work because there aren't any; in others, there are no curtains because... that's right: there aren't any! And yet, in the entire area for kilometers around, this is the best there is.

They make sandwiches for the travelers on the road, wrapping them in foil. True, there's a lot of bread and not much sausage, but the gesture itself—the thoughtfulness—is important. For some reason, they don't always offer eggs in the morning; maybe it's a cultural thing. And there's an Alabai dog on a leash. The leash is short, probably to teach it to keep its place; it's a lot of nonsense.

The top floor has the best room, where from 11:00 PM you can see all the stars in the world accessible in this hemisphere. You want to look at the stars again and again.

And when I think about this, I envy all the new guests at Ropojan 🔭🌌

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ A superb stop in Theth!

After arriving in Theth by bus, we spent the day hiking to Grunas Waterfall and then to the Blue Eye viewpoint – a beautiful day of walking.

In the evening, we arrived at Kullat E Sadri Lukes, our accommodation for the night. A wonderful discovery! The place is peaceful, authentic, and situated in a magnificent setting in the heart of the mountains.
We received a very warm welcome from Maria, who was very friendly and welcoming. The accommodation is about 3 km from Theth and, more importantly, quite close to the starting point of the Theth-Valbona long-distance hike, which is really convenient when you have to set off on foot again the next morning.
After our day at Grunas and the Blue Eye, it was exactly the kind of place we were looking for to rest before tackling the trek to Valbona. Authentic accommodation, a very warm welcome, and an ideal location for hikers. We highly recommend this place! 🇦🇱⛰️🥾

google_reviews.author: Borislav Ivanov
google_reviews.text:
Feels like you're visiting your Albanian grandmother. Very different from what you'll find in the otherwise somewhat overcrowded and touristy Thethi village.

Exceptional hospitality! Homemade food with local products. Dinner is exactly at 18:30 every day, guests sit together in the dining room to eat what has been just cooked for them.

Rooms are spacious and exceptionally clean, with modern bathroom with plenty of hot water. The houses are traditional stone-made, neighboring the farm. Happy cows, hens, pigs are out for the day and come back for the night.

The place has an amazing view, one which cannot fit in photos. The house is surrounded by 800-meter walls and 2000+ meter peaks. The road is unpaved and bumpy for the last kilometers, but very much worth it.

Maria is a great host!
Reminds me of my dear grandmother Maria — for her the most important was that nobody stayed outside, and bellies were full for the next day adventures.

To Maria We arrived very late night around 22 pm. She offered us right away a place to stay — although she already had a full house with guests.
Although the dinner had long been served, she put us a soup on the fire.
We were very tired and hungry after a hardcore downhill hiking

I really recommend if you want some clean and honest stay. Around you will be free walking sheep, cows and silent guests.

The breakfast was astonishing: homemade honey, tasty bread, olive oil, jam…

There is a lot of woodcraft around, that makes you feel in a gallery! Go visit!

Second, during the first one hour drive the driver was constantly checking his phone instead of looking at the road which is very steep and rocky. This is insane and made me feel very unsafe. Third, we left at 11:30 from the guesthouse, by 12:30 we were still in theth because the driver was constantly stopping to pick up ppl/stuff, which wasn’t informed in beginning, so I arrived shkoder 1hr late and I have to change my plans. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at Butjina Mani. The accommodation offers a stunning view of the mountains. There's a hairdryer, hot showers, and a heater in the room.

We especially appreciated how much quieter, more idyllic, and more authentic it is up there than down in the valley. You experience traditional mountain life much more directly, and the atmosphere is simply special. Despite this tranquility, Theth is only about a 30-minute walk away. The path is a pleasant stroll with beautiful views and isn't overly steep.

Lola is an incredibly warm and welcoming host. She cooked for us with great care and attention. Breakfast was outstanding, the best of our trip: with fresh milk, homemade butter, jam, and much more.

The accommodation is located directly on the trails leading to Valbona and the Peja Pass.

A quick note about getting there: There are two possible routes to the accommodation. We highly recommend taking the route through the center of Theth and across the wooden bridge there. The gravel road there is significantly more pleasant and less steep than the alternative that Google Maps unfortunately suggests.

google_reviews.text: We stayed here for 3 days. What fantastic people the owners are; they help you with everything and think of everything. We also ate here for 3 days, and it was delicious!

google_reviews.author: Anouk
google_reviews.text: First of all, the view is amazing. Had a wonderful stay. For a small fee, we were also able to enjoy the host's cooking skills. Highly recommended!

google_reviews.author: Ilias zch
google_reviews.text: One of the best places to stay in Thethi, easily accessible by car. The staff was very kind, helpful and willing to help us with anything we needed. The food (breakfast and dinner) in the restaurant of the accommodation was delicious. Also, the accommodation has the best view of the Theth valley and the surrounding mountains. Theth is a paradise on earth and Royal Land has the most beautiful balcony! See you soon

google_reviews.author: Kemal D.
google_reviews.text: Highly recommended for nice service, generous portions and delicious food. We've had a lovely dinner after our exhausting Valbone to Theth hike and couldn't wish for something better. Thank you many times!

google_reviews.author: Phil Richardson
google_reviews.text: This wasn't our first choice when booking but how lucky were we to book here. Honestly, after walking around thiscarea for 3 days, this is the perfect location. So close to Theth Village but away from the hustle and bustle of that busy scene. So quiet here and only 10 minutes walk along the stream to the Village. One major plus is the family owners of at least 3 generations working this place. They are so welcoming and helpful. This should be your first choice when visiting the Albanian Alps in Theth area. Thank you Royal Land

google_reviews.author: Deanna y Brian
google_reviews.text:
The place is incredible, the landscapes are beautiful, waking up to the imposing sight of such a mountain is amazing.
The room is very nice; in my opinion, it could use some air conditioning, but I understand that due to the limited electricity, air conditioning would complicate everyone's stay. The bathroom is fine and functional. What I want to highlight most is the hospitality of Astrid and her wife, which makes the stay unforgettable. In fact, it makes you want to stay even longer.
Astrid is a very attentive and kind person. We didn't have much contact with her husband, but it wasn't necessary since she cooked for us during our stay. Someone who makes things taste so delicious only has one ingredient that makes it possible: she cooks with love.
The lunch and breakfast are both worth eating there; you really sit down to eat and leave completely full. The food is incredible. And once again, I must mention the service. We didn't have a car, and going down to the city was a bit more difficult. That's when we asked if there was a possibility of having lunch. We really hate eating sandwiches, and their response was a huge salad plus eggs, cheese, and chorizo—more than enough! Simply thank you for your hospitality; I recommend it a thousand times over.

google_reviews.author: CM K
google_reviews.text: A beautiful inn with a stunning view, run by a lovely family. Dinner was delicious too!

google_reviews.author: jean vieville
google_reviews.text:
Astrit and her family gave us a wonderful welcome and were exceptional hosts throughout our stay, thank you 🙏

Special mention for dinner, which was absolutely incredible: delicious, generous, and authentic. I highly recommend having it if you have the chance!

A big thank you to Astrit and her entire family for their kindness and hospitality. A truly wonderful experience!

google_reviews.author: Emilia
google_reviews.text: A fantastic place to stay, which we unanimously called the highlight of our trip to Albania. We received a super friendly welcome from the owner's son, the room is modern and clean, and the view is simply unbeatable! We would come back anytime.
